title: Autoscale regression sentinel and remediation initiative
creator: Miguel Ramos
description: Summary: On 2025-11-02 we observed a sustained throughput shortfall across several Dedicated customer pools (US-East-1 and EU-West-1). The autoscaler stopped provisioning additional nodes at expected thresholds, headroom collapsed, and latency SLOs for tail percentiles were breached for ~42 minutes for affected customers. Impact: multiple enterprise customers experienced elevated 95/99th latency and intermittent throttling; one customer reported degraded user-facing features. Root cause: a regression in the cluster-autoscaler policy introduced during a roll of the scheduling controller (changeet A-1137) altered the eviction/batch_accept heuristics, which caused the autoscaler to believe pending queue length was glassed (stale) when KV-cache warmup spikes occurred. In certain load patterns this suppressed scale-up decisions. Contributing factors: insufficient sentinel coverage for 'scale_decision_skew' and missing threshold for sustained pending_count over 30s; rollout gating did not trigger canary abort when the autoscaler hit degraded metrics. Detection: incident alerted via internal SLO alarm 'dedicated.pool.available_headroom' combined with customer-reported errors. The on-call runbook steps were followed to triage, but initial mitigations were manual and ad-hoc. This ticket tracks the triage, remediation, hotfix, and long-term mitigations to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2025-11-02 09:12 - On-call (Liang Chen): Pager received for elevated 99th latency in pool-dedicated-us-east. Began triage; alerted infra and product owners.

2025-11-02 09:20 - Asha Patel: Confirmed autoscaler not launching nodes despite pending queue growth. Applied emergency policy to force-burst one 8-node augmentation for affected pools (temporary mitigation).
2025-11-02 10:01 - Miguel Ramos: Identified recent changeet A-1137 in scheduling controller as correlated. Reverted scheduling patch in canary; observed autoscale decisions resume in canary pool.
2025-11-02 11:30 - Post-incident: Temporary augmentation turned down after hotfix published. Customer success notified and incident summary prepared for affected accounts.
2025-11-05 15:43 - Design review: Agreed to add a sentinel metric and dashboard for 'scale_decision_skew' and introduce a 30s sustained pending_count threshold in autoscaler heuristics.
2025-11-12 13:12 - Infra lead (Rita Gomez): Hotfix PR merged; autoscaler behavior corrected to ignore transient KV-cache warmup spikes when evaluating scale decisions.
2025-11-18 09:05 - SRE (Omar Malik): Runbook updated with emergency augmentation steps and clarified escalation paths; added explicit rollback steps for scheduling changes.
steps_taken: Applied emergency augmentation to affected Dedicated pools to restore headroom (manual burst of reserved nodes).
Reverted scheduling controller changeet A-1137 in canary and observed autoscaler return to expected decisions in canary pool within 8 minutes.
Rolled hotfix to autoscaler heuristics to add sustained pending_count window and ignore KV-cache warmup noise.
Ran gradual rollout of hotfix across regions with extended canary metrics and abort gating.
Notified Customer Success and impacted customers; created post-incident customer-facing summary and credits where applicable.
action_items: AI-1: Add sentinel metric 'scale_decision_skew' and surface it in the Redwood Console per-route dashboards. Owner: Asha Patel. Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-11-28.
AI-2: Harden autoscaler policy: implement sustained-window (30s) threshold for pending_count and KV-cache warmup tolerance. Owner: Liang Chen. Estimate: 5. Due: 2025-11-20.
AI-3: Update CI/CD rollout gating to automatically abort if autoscale-related canary metrics degrade >10% for 5 minutes. Owner: Rita Gomez. Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-12-05.
AI-4: Add synthetic load tests into dedicated pool staging to exercise KV-cache warmup and autoscale decisions pre-merge. Owner: SRE Team. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-01-15.
AI-5: Create postmortem blameless write-up and customer RCA deck; schedule review with CSM and Sales. Owner: Miguel Ramos. Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-11-14.
